concept.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
concept.title: RAG: retrieve evidence, then generate
concept.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation finds relevant private knowledge for each question, places that evidence in the prompt, and asks a language model to answer from it.
concept.problem: A language model cannot reliably answer from current, private, or organization-specific knowledge that was not available during training.

goals: explain the end-to-end RAG data path
separate retrieval failures from generation failures

nodes.label: Enterprise Data
nodes.caption: documents and records
nodes.description: The private source material that should ground answers, such as policies, tickets, or product documentation.

nodes.label: User Question
nodes.caption: the live request
nodes.description: The user's question, plus identity and authorization context used to restrict retrieval.

nodes.label: Chunk and Enrich
nodes.caption: prepare searchable units
nodes.description: Documents are split into useful passages and enriched with source, date, ownership, and access metadata.

nodes.label: Query Embedding
nodes.caption: represent the question
nodes.description: An embedding model converts the question into a vector suitable for semantic search.

nodes.label: Embedding Model
nodes.caption: represent each chunk
nodes.description: The same embedding space turns document chunks into vectors that can be compared with query vectors.

nodes.label: Vector Store
nodes.caption: vectors + metadata
nodes.description: The index stores chunk vectors, source text, metadata, and permissions used during retrieval.

nodes.label: Retriever
nodes.caption: find allowed evidence
nodes.description: The retriever searches for relevant chunks, applies access filters, and may rerank candidates.

nodes.label: Prompt Builder
nodes.caption: question + evidence
nodes.description: The prompt builder combines instructions, the user question, and retrieved passages within the model context window.

nodes.label: Language Model
nodes.caption: generate from context
nodes.description: The language model synthesizes an answer from the supplied question and evidence; it does not perform retrieval itself.

nodes.label: Grounded Answer
nodes.caption: response with citations
nodes.description: The final response should be traceable to retrieved sources and should abstain when evidence is insufficient.

groups.label: Offline Knowledge Preparation
groups.description: The indexing path that turns governed source content into searchable representations.

groups.label: Retrieval
groups.description: The online search boundary where relevance and authorization determine which evidence is returned.

groups.label: Generation
groups.description: The online synthesis path that combines the question and evidence for the language model.

chapters.title: Prepare private knowledge
chapters.explanation: Before questions arrive, source data is split into meaningful chunks, enriched with metadata, embedded, and stored in a searchable index.

chapters.title: Represent the live question
chapters.explanation: At request time, the user's question is embedded into the same vector space as the indexed chunks.

chapters.title: Retrieve relevant, allowed evidence
chapters.explanation: The retriever searches the vector store, filters by the user's permissions, and returns the strongest passages. Retrieval quality sets the ceiling for the final answer.
takeaways: Relevance and authorization are separate filters
Inspect retrieved chunks before blaming the model

chapters.title: Build a grounded prompt
chapters.explanation: The prompt builder combines the original question, instructions, and retrieved evidence without exceeding the model's context window.

chapters.title: Generate and cite the answer
chapters.explanation: The language model synthesizes a response from the supplied context. The application should attach citations and abstain when the evidence is weak.

roleRelevance.title: Why this matters for a Solutions Architect
points: Separate the offline indexing architecture from the online request path.
Place authorization filtering inside retrieval, not only in the user interface.
Diagnose retrieval relevance before tuning prompts or replacing the language model.
Define citation and abstention behavior as product requirements, not presentation details.

contextCards.title: Quality levers
points: Chunking and metadata determine what can be found.
Prompt construction and model choice determine synthesis.

contextCards.title: Security boundary
points: Propagate user identity into each retrieval request.
Filter source records before they enter model context.
Keep citations so access and provenance can be audited.

contextCards.title: Common failure modes
points: No useful chunk: indexing or retrieval problem.
Useful chunk omitted from prompt: orchestration problem.
Good evidence, wrong synthesis: generation problem.
